options.name: Therapeutic Alliance and Engagement
options.description: Therapist builds rapport, fosters trust, and encourages open communication to support collaboration throughout therapy.

goal.objective: Develop a strong, safe, and collaborative foundation for effective therapeutic work.

success_levels.ideal: Patient feels understood, safe, and motivated; participates actively and shares openly.
success_levels.acceptable: Patient expresses some willingness to engage, with moderate trust and participation.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Patient feels disconnected, mistrustful, or unengaged, blocking therapeutic progress.

goal.reward_hint: Patient expresses feeling understood, participates willingly, or references the strength of the alliance.

states: Initial contact and early sessions
Patient expresses hesitancy, mistrust, or low engagement
Therapeutic relationship strains or ruptures emerge
Throughout all sessions for maintenance

options.name: Psychoeducation and Therapy Orientation
options.description: Therapist explains CBT principles, session structure, dispels myths, and normalizes emotional and psychological experiences.

goal.objective: Increase patient understanding of CBT, foster engagement, and correct misconceptions.

success_levels.ideal: Patient accurately understands CBT concepts and rationale, feels reassured, and participates actively.
success_levels.acceptable: Patient shows basic understanding and reduced misconceptions, and is open to starting therapy.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Patient remains confused or resistant due to misunderstanding or stigma.

goal.reward_hint: Patient articulates CBT principles, expresses reduced shame or curiosity, and asks relevant questions.

states: Therapy is beginning or transitioning to a new focus
Patient is unfamiliar or uncertain about CBT/diagnosis
Misconceptions, stigma, shame, or anxiety about therapy are evident

options.name: Assessment, Diagnosis, and Case Formulation
options.description: Therapist gathers information on symptoms, personal history, context, and risk to clarify presenting problems and form an individualized CBT case conceptualization.

goal.objective: Achieve a shared, clear understanding of patient’s difficulties and conceptual model to guide treatment.

success_levels.ideal: Comprehensive, collaboratively-developed formulation with clear targets for intervention.
success_levels.acceptable: Basic understanding of problems and relevant patterns sufficient to start planning.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Problems remain unclear, fragmented, or formulation is missing/inaccurate.

goal.reward_hint: Therapist and patient reference the formulation and agree on targets for intervention.

states: Intake and early sessions
Symptoms or history are unclear or complex
When planning or revising treatment targets

options.name: Agenda, Goal Setting, and Action Planning
options.description: Therapist and patient collaboratively set session agendas, prioritize treatment goals, and develop actionable plans for intervention.

goal.objective: Establish shared goals and clear session plans to organize and focus therapy.

success_levels.ideal: Patient and therapist agree on specific, measurable goals and action steps; work proceeds collaboratively.
success_levels.acceptable: Goals are moderately specific and session structure is present but may lack full clarity.
success_levels.unsuccessful: No clear goals or agenda; patient feels uninvolved or the plan is unfocused.

goal.reward_hint: Patient articulates and selects goals, actively participates in setting agenda and plans.

states: Start of every session
Following assessment/psychoeducation
When motivation or direction is unclear

options.name: Cognitive Interventions: Identification and Restructuring
options.description: Therapist helps the patient identify automatic thoughts, cognitive distortions, and maladaptive beliefs, and uses Socratic techniques to challenge and modify them.

goal.objective: Reduce distress and maladaptive behaviors by restructuring dysfunctional cognitive patterns.

success_levels.ideal: Patient regularly identifies, evaluates, and modifies automatic thoughts and beliefs with increased cognitive flexibility.
success_levels.acceptable: Patient recognizes some patterns and engages in restructuring with therapist support.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Patient is unable or unwilling to identify or challenge problematic thoughts.

goal.reward_hint: Patient articulates automatic thoughts, participates in cognitive tasks, and verbalizes new perspectives.

states: Patient reports distressing emotions or behaviors tied to thoughts
Cognitive restructuring or belief modification phase
Persistent negative thinking or rigid beliefs present

options.name: Core Beliefs and Schema Work
options.description: Therapist assists patient to identify, evaluate, and modify core beliefs and schemas underlying persistent difficulties.

goal.objective: Restructure negative core beliefs and build more flexible, adaptive self-concepts.

success_levels.ideal: Patient identifies and changes core beliefs, adopting healthier alternatives and demonstrating lasting change.
success_levels.acceptable: Patient becomes aware of core beliefs and starts practicing new perspectives.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Core beliefs remain unexamined or unchanged.

goal.reward_hint: Patient discusses core beliefs, practices new ones, and behavior reflects change.

states: Surface restructuring has limited effect
Longstanding patterns traced to global beliefs
Later therapy stages focused on underlying schemas

options.name: Behavioral Activation, Experimentation, and Skills Training
options.description: Therapist uses graded activity scheduling, behavioral experiments, and skills training to reduce avoidance, increase adaptive behaviors, and improve functioning.

goal.objective: Decrease avoidance and increase positive behavior, learning, and coping skills.

success_levels.ideal: Patient completes planned experiments and activities, develops new skills, and benefits are generalized.
success_levels.acceptable: Patient attempts activities/experiments and practices some skills, with partial progress.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Patient avoids activities or fails to practice, resulting in persistent symptoms.

goal.reward_hint: Patient completes tasks, describes outcomes, and demonstrates skill use in session and daily life.

states: Symptoms related to inactivity, avoidance, or skill deficits
Cognitive interventions alone are insufficient
Patient is ready to test beliefs or build new behaviors

options.name: Exposure and Response Prevention
options.description: Therapist and patient collaboratively design and implement graded exposure to feared or avoided situations and guide prevention of safety behaviors.

goal.objective: Reduce avoidance and anxiety by increasing experiential learning and disconfirming maladaptive beliefs.

success_levels.ideal: Patient completes hierarchically graded exposures, reduces anxiety/avoidance, and acquires adaptive responses.
success_levels.acceptable: Patient attempts exposure tasks with some decrease in distress or avoidance.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Patient continues to avoid feared situations, uses safety behaviors, or increases anxiety.

goal.reward_hint: Patient completes and reflects on exposures and reports decreased distress or more adaptive functioning.

states: Patient presents with avoidance, anxiety, phobia, or OCD symptoms
When reducing avoidance or testing beliefs is needed

options.name: Skills Generalization, Homework, and Progress Review
options.description: Therapist assigns practice tasks between sessions, monitors progress, addresses obstacles, and reinforces skill development.

goal.objective: Generalize CBT skills to real-life situations and foster independent coping.

success_levels.ideal: Patient completes homework consistently, applies skills independently, and reports gains.
success_levels.acceptable: Patient attempts homework with therapist support and shows partial skill generalization.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Patient avoids or does not complete homework and skills do not generalize.

goal.reward_hint: Patient brings records/homework, reports skill use outside session, and discusses successes and challenges.

states: Between sessions to consolidate skills
When monitoring application in daily life
Troubleshooting noncompliance or limited progress

options.name: Relapse Prevention and Termination Planning
options.description: Therapist and patient prepare for therapy ending by consolidating skills, anticipating risk, and developing maintenance plans.

goal.objective: Enable patient to sustain gains, prevent relapse, and apply skills independently post-therapy.

success_levels.ideal: Patient develops and practices a relapse prevention plan, maintains progress, and expresses readiness for independence.
success_levels.acceptable: Patient understands risks, uses basic strategies, and requires minimal reminders.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Patient is unprepared, lacks a plan, or regresses when therapy ends.

goal.reward_hint: Patient can articulate prevention strategies, self-monitor, and demonstrates flexible coping.

states: Later/termination phase of therapy
Following substantial progress
Patient is concerned about setbacks, relapse, or future risks

options.name: Crisis Management and Safety Planning
options.description: Therapist directly addresses acutely increased risk (e.g., suicidality or emergency needs) through focused assessment, stabilization, and plan development.

goal.objective: Manage acute risk and ensure patient safety through rapid assessment, collaborative planning, and emergency intervention if needed.

success_levels.ideal: Risk is identified, managed actively, and safety is secured with a clear plan.
success_levels.acceptable: Risk is reduced or monitored; plans are in place for ongoing safety.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Risk persists or worsens; safety plan is absent or not followed.

goal.reward_hint: Patient follows safety plan, risk is reduced, or therapist takes appropriate emergency actions.

states: Patient reports suicidal ideation, self-harm risk, or acute emergency
Ongoing risk factors surface during treatment
Crisis or emergencies occur in session

options.name: Ongoing Progress Monitoring and Troubleshooting
options.description: Therapist regularly tracks symptom change, adapts interventions, and engages in collaborative problem-solving of obstacles and setbacks.

goal.objective: Ensure effective treatment by tracking progress, adjusting strategies, and resolving barriers.

success_levels.ideal: Symptoms and goals are tracked, obstacles are addressed, and treatment adapts to promote continuous improvement.
success_levels.acceptable: Progress is monitored; treatment adjustments are made for partial improvement.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Progress stalls or regresses without responsive troubleshooting.

goal.reward_hint: Documented progress, intervention changes, and specific problem-solving observed in therapy.

states: When symptoms do not improve as expected
Barriers to engagement, skill use, or homework occur
Significant life changes disrupt progress

Current emotional state and its intensity, including shifts and predominant affect (e.g., anxiety, depression, anger, guilt).
Strength or severity of emotional responses or distress. Used to track intervention impact, risk, and session pacing.
Overall intensity and fluctuation of target psychiatric symptoms (e.g., depression, anxiety). Guides formulation and treatment.
Extent to which symptoms or behaviors interfere with social, occupational, educational, or daily functioning.
Type, presence, and frequency of faulty thinking patterns (e.g., catastrophizing, overgeneralization, black-and-white thinking). Informs cognitive restructuring.
Patient's ability to identify, reflect on, and understand their own thoughts, emotions, and behavioral patterns.
Patient's willingness, motivation, and openness to engage in change processes and new strategies.
Strength, quality, and trust in the working relationship between therapist and patient, including collaboration and conflict.
Patient's activity, willingness, and collaboration during sessions and with treatment tasks.
Degree of completion, quality of engagement, and reflection with therapy homework, assignments, or behavioral experiments.
Presence, frequency, and reliance on avoidance and safety behaviors/rituals aimed at reducing perceived threat or distress.
Movement toward therapy/treatment goals, including behavioral activation, symptom reduction, and completion of tasks.
Presence, quality, and helpfulness of patient's relationships, support network, and interpersonal connections.
Frequency and effectiveness of adaptive or maladaptive coping skills used to manage distress, including problem-solving and emotional regulation.
Influence of comorbid diagnoses or symptoms (e.g., depression, social anxiety, chronic pain, substance misuse) on session engagement and progress.

states.Variable Name: Relapse Risk and Early Warning Signs
states.Description: Presence and intensity of early warning signs or risk factors for relapse or deterioration. Used for monitoring and prevention.
Presence, intensity, and change in suicidal thoughts, intent, planning, and behaviors. Guides safety planning.
Internal and external barriers (practical, emotional, motivational, or situational) interfering with progress, engagement, or skill application.
Degree of shift in conviction or emotional response following behavioral experiments or corrective experiences.
Extent to which acquired cognitions and behaviors transfer to situations outside of session. Indicates real-world impact.
Self-reported or observed emotional discomfort or distress, including SUDs ratings. Used to inform safety and intervention selection.
Patient's preparedness, willingness, and commitment to take action, explore new strategies, or participate in exposures/advanced interventions.
Therapist's own emotional responses and their potential influence on the session.
Overall assessment of patient's well-being and satisfaction with life, reflecting symptoms and functional impact.
Quality, onset, duration, and disruptions in sleep, including restfulness or insomnia.
Somatic symptoms related to mood or anxiety (e.g., sleep, appetite, energy, agitation).
Consideration of individual cultural, developmental, and identity factors relevant to therapy engagement and alliance.
Ability to retain, recall, and apply CBT concepts and skills, highlighting barriers and need for adaptations.
Whether patient's attention is self-focused or externally directed. Guides intervention selection.
External circumstances or recent life events impacting engagement, such as trauma, financial stress, or loss.
Degree of agreement or discrepancy between therapist and patient on goals, analysis, and evidence.

static_dimensions.description: Captures age, gender, race/ethnicity, marital/family status, education, employment, roles, sexuality, cultural background, religion, and the broader social environment. Provides life context, shapes relevant stressors, influences disclosure comfort, and impacts engagement or interpretation of therapy.
static_dimensions.value_guidance: Summarize the person's demographic details, identity, living situation, cultural influences, roles (e.g., parent, student), and any relevant social network or identity-linked considerations.

static_dimensions.description: Captures significant life events, upbringing, early experiences (e.g., trauma, adversity), family context, history of anxiety or mood symptoms, and the developmental stage at onset of key issues. Provides background for current beliefs, vulnerability patterns, and triggers.
static_dimensions.value_guidance: Describe formative experiences, family background, critical life events, early adversities, age/context of symptom onset, and their lasting impact. Note information gaps if unknown.

static_dimensions.description: Captures enduring, deeply held beliefs, schemas, or cognitive frameworks about self, others, and the world—including habitual appraisals about safety, worth, responsibility, emotion, and control. Influences symptom expression, resistance, and therapy focus.
static_dimensions.value_guidance: Summarize key core beliefs, cognitive themes (e.g., danger, unlovability, hopelessness), patterns of interpretation, and domains these beliefs affect. Reference specific language, examples, or direct statements where possible.

static_dimensions.description: Characterizes habitual trait tendencies (e.g., neuroticism, trait anxiety, introversion), interpersonal style, and general communication or disclosure patterns (e.g., openness, guardedness, self-awareness). Informs alliance, prediction of engagement, and tailoring interventions.
static_dimensions.value_guidance: Describe enduring personality features, baseline emotion patterns, typical communication style, openness or reticence, and context-specific communication strengths or limitations.

static_dimensions.description: Lists lifetime and current diagnoses, symptom course and severity, comorbid psychiatric or medical conditions (including cognitive/formal diagnoses, substance use, trauma), and history of chronicity or remission. Aids in prioritizing treatment and adapting approaches.
static_dimensions.value_guidance: List main current/past diagnoses, comorbidities, symptom courses (chronic/intermittent), and impact on functioning. Add relevant medical/psychiatric factors as described.

static_dimensions.description: Captures traumatic exposures, type, timing, severity, perceived meaning, and personal impact. Includes whether trauma was interpersonal, situational, or repeated, and any specific index event relevant to current difficulties.
static_dimensions.value_guidance: Describe relevant trauma history, nature/timing/context of exposures, the patient’s interpretation and willingness to disclose, and specify any index event if known or if avoidance impedes elaboration.

static_dimensions.dimension_name: Habitual Coping Strategies and Safety Behaviors
static_dimensions.description: Describes routinely used strategies for managing stress or distress—e.g., avoidance, reassurance seeking, ritualizing, suppression, withdrawal, substance use, checking, perfectionism, aggression. Indicates automatic responses and relapse risk areas.
static_dimensions.value_guidance: List habitual response patterns (avoidance, safety behaviors, reassurance seeking), typical rationales, exceptions or context-specific use, and perceived effectiveness. Describe coping flexibility or rigidity.

static_dimensions.description: Summarizes enduring strengths (supportive relationships, problem-solving abilities, openness, resilience, skills), available social/practical supports, and chronic barriers (e.g., financial, cognitive, medical, logistical, occupational, or technology constraints). Highlights assets to leverage and stable challenges.
static_dimensions.value_guidance: Outline practical or psychological strengths, available support systems (family, friends, peers), coping resources, and any longstanding barriers or constraints affecting participation or progress.

static_dimensions.description: Captures prior experiences with therapy (CBT or others), medication use, engagement/adherence patterns, outcomes (including relapse or nonresponse), attitudes toward treatment, and preferences or concerns about approaches.
static_dimensions.value_guidance: List previous therapies, medication trials, outcomes, adherence issues, side effects, attitudes, and stated preferences, noting any history of skepticism, dropouts, or treatment motivation.

static_dimensions.description: Describes enduring life goals, values, motivations for engaging in therapy or change, approach/avoidance orientation, and baseline readiness for intervention or exposure work.
static_dimensions.value_guidance: Articulate stated therapy goals, valued life domains, motivation for change (or ambivalence), avoidance/engagement stance, and contextual priorities or conflicts.

static_dimensions.description: Identifies specific anxiety-provoking, avoided, or symptom-triggering situations and the meaning associated with them. Useful for guiding exposure and interpreting episodes.
static_dimensions.value_guidance: List triggers and avoided situations, meaning or significance attached, and circumstances that amplify or reduce impact (e.g., presence of support, public vs. private).

static_dimensions.description: Describes intellectual functioning, communication, learning style, memory, and ability to engage with psychoeducation or new tasks. Informs adaptation of therapy and education.
static_dimensions.value_guidance: Describe cognitive/learning strengths and limits, communication skills, and need for adaptations in therapy materials or interventions.

dynamic_dimensions.description: Captures momentary or sessional emotional state (e.g., anxiety, sadness, anger, shame, hope, numbness), its conversational relevance, and observable or reported affect. Options reflect dominant or co-existing emotions; 'unknown' when not evident.
dynamic_dimensions.update_condition: Add or remove emotions based on verbal or nonverbal cues, self-report, session observations, and explicit statement. Options may co-occur; set to 'unknown' if not reported or inferable.

dynamic_dimensions.description: Tracks current severity of key symptoms (anxiety, depression, panic, OCD, distress) as observed or reported. Reflects impact for the present session/context and informs session pacing or intervention need.
dynamic_dimensions.update_condition: Switch when self-report, standardized measures, behavioral observation, or explicit evidence indicates a change; retain previous if not clearly altered; use 'unknown' when not available.

dynamic_dimensions.description: Captures the nature and course of presenting symptoms (improved, worsened, fluctuating, unchanged) or active comorbidities in session. May be expressed in terms of diagnostic status (e.g., PTSD, dissociation, suicidality) or general symptom shifts.
dynamic_dimensions.update_condition: Update when direct evidence (self-report, worksheet, observation) supports a change in current status; retain if stable; set 'unknown' if not assessed.

dynamic_dimensions.description: Represents present stance toward session participation, therapeutic tasks, or exposure assignments (committed, ambivalent, resistant, disengaged, highly motivated, passive compliance). Informs intervention pacing and engagement strategy.
dynamic_dimensions.update_condition: Change with evidence (engagement, statements, behavior), including increased or decreased willingness or resistance. Retain if no update. Use 'unknown' if not observable.

dynamic_dimensions.description: Reflects degree and current quality of involvement in therapeutic activities, discussion, and tasks (e.g., active, passive, avoidant, distracted, resistant, supportive to others). Especially relevant for group or in-session dynamics.
dynamic_dimensions.update_condition: Update based on observed or reported behavior, willingness to participate, engagement with exercises, or feedback. Options may co-occur; set to 'unknown' if insufficient data.

dynamic_dimensions.description: Tracks currently observed or reported coping methods or avoidance behaviors being used in session or recent context (e.g., avoidance, reassurance seeking, exposure, cognitive skills, substance use), including adaptive/maladaptive distinctions.
dynamic_dimensions.update_condition: Add or remove based on explicit report, observation, or worksheet review. Options may overlap; set 'unknown' if not assessed.

dynamic_dimensions.dimension_name: Cognitive Flexibility, Automatic Thoughts, and Reappraisal
dynamic_dimensions.description: Captures state of thinking in session—degree of rigidity, use of cognitive restructuring, presence of negative automatic thoughts or schema activation, catastrophic thinking, or acceptance.
dynamic_dimensions.update_condition: Modify when patient demonstrates or reports changes in cognitive approach, activation of certain themes/schemas, or attempts at restructuring. Multiple may apply; use 'unknown' if absent.

dynamic_dimensions.description: Describes current attentional focus—internal (body, thoughts), external (environment, social), balanced, distracted, or symptom scanning. Relevant to anxiety maintenance and session strategies.
dynamic_dimensions.update_condition: Update as per observed attentional shifts, self-report, or session cues; multiple styles may be present; select 'unknown' if not evident.

dynamic_dimensions.description: Reflects current capacity to recognize, describe, and reflect on symptoms, beliefs, or maladaptive patterns—ranging from absent, vague, through developing to advanced insight.
dynamic_dimensions.update_condition: Switch option based on session evidence (self-monitoring reports, insight about errors, behavioral tracking); update with increased/decreased awareness; otherwise, retain or 'unknown' if unclear.

dynamic_dimensions.description: Represents current openness or reluctance to share emotional experiences, personal history, or symptoms and participate in therapeutic discussion. Options range from fully open to guarded, concealment, selective disclosure, or avoidance.
dynamic_dimensions.update_condition: Select based on observed sharing, willingness to discuss sensitive topics, avoidance, or situational openness; 'unknown' if unassessed.

dynamic_dimensions.dimension_name: Therapeutic Alliance and Support Network Involvement
dynamic_dimensions.description: Captures current quality of alliance with therapist or group (strong, tenuous, rupture, repair) and involvement of family/support network (supportive, interfering, withdrawing, conflictual). Informs session strategy and risk of disengagement.
dynamic_dimensions.update_condition: Switch on evidence of change in rapport, feedback, support involvement, or trust reported/observed in session. Use 'unknown' if not discussed.

dynamic_dimensions.description: Tracks response to therapeutic assignments or homework (e.g., exposures, thought records)—degree of compliance, avoidance, minimization, or adaptation.
dynamic_dimensions.update_condition: Change based on session review, patient explanation, or observation; retain prior state if unchanged; set to 'unknown' if unreported.

dynamic_dimensions.dimension_name: Generalization and Maintenance of Therapy Gains
dynamic_dimensions.description: Indicates whether therapeutic gains are restricted to sessions, generalized to outside contexts, sustained, or lost (relapse). Guides focus for relapse prevention.
dynamic_dimensions.update_condition: Switch when evidence of change in generalization appears via self-report, observation, or feedback; set 'unknown' if not evaluated.

dynamic_dimensions.description: Captures current medication use (starting, maintaining, tapering, withdrawal, side effects, or no medication) and impact on session or functioning.
dynamic_dimensions.update_condition: Update as per patient/clinician report or observed effects; remove/add states as medication status changes; set 'unknown' if not discussed.

options.name: Attitude and Belief Assessment
options.description: Assess and profile the persuadee’s attitudes, beliefs, attitude structure, certainty, ambivalence, and underlying functions prior to tailored persuasion.

goal.objective: Accurately characterize the persuadee’s attitudes, beliefs, and underlying motives to inform tailored persuasive interventions.

success_levels.ideal: Comprehensive and accurate mapping of relevant attitudes, beliefs, certainty, ambivalence, and functions, enabling precise message adaptation.
success_levels.acceptable: Major attitude and belief features identified at a level sufficient for basic message tailoring.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Lack of or inaccurate assessment leads to mismatched or ineffective persuasive strategies.

goal.reward_hint: Persuader demonstrates a nuanced understanding of persuadee's attitudes, beliefs, and functions; interventions are tailored and contextually appropriate.

states: Persuadee's attitudes, beliefs, or preferences are unknown or unclear.
Beginning of persuasion dialogue or planning.
Need to assess structure, certainty, ambivalence, or function of attitudes.

options.name: Tailoring Message Content and Framing
options.description: Adapt persuasive messaging to match the persuadee’s attitude functions, motives, beliefs, and preferences for optimal impact.

goal.objective: Increase persuasive effectiveness by aligning message content, framing, and style to the persuadee’s dominant motives and attitude structure.

success_levels.ideal: Message is perfectly matched to key functions, values, or determinants, maximizing persuasive impact.
success_levels.acceptable: Message aligns with some relevant characteristics, improving receptivity.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Message is mismatched, ignored, or rejected; triggers resistance.

goal.reward_hint: Persuadee’s engagement, involvement, and positive processing are increased; message is viewed as relevant.

states: Attitude functions, beliefs, or motivational basis have been identified.
Time to construct the intervention or select content and framing.
Generic strategies are not sufficient.

options.name: Engagement and Persuasive Message Delivery
options.description: Present the main persuasive content using tactical structures, narratives, rationales, sequential requests, and strategic framing.

goal.objective: Deliver persuasive content that achieves attitudinal or behavioral shift toward the intended goal.

success_levels.ideal: Persuadee is engaged and favorably evaluates the message, leading to desired change.
success_levels.acceptable: Persuadee attends to the message and considers the proposal.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Persuadee disregards, resists, or reacts negatively to the message.

goal.reward_hint: Evidence of persuadee engagement, elaboration, or positive attitudinal movement.

states: Persuadee is primed or ready for new information.
Message is tailored and ready for delivery.
Initial assessment and tailoring phases have passed.

options.name: Reciprocity Initiation
options.description: Initiate dialogue by creating a sense of indebtedness in the persuadee through unsolicited favors or concessions.

goal.objective: Trigger the persuadee's desire to reciprocate and increase compliance by establishing obligation.

success_levels.ideal: Persuadee feels indebted and predisposed to comply with subsequent requests.
success_levels.acceptable: Persuadee acknowledges the favor and exhibits moderate inclination to reciprocate.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Persuadee does not value or recognize the favor.

goal.reward_hint: Signs of gratitude, indebtedness, or willingness to reciprocate.

states: Beginning of interaction.
Persuadee has not yet received a request.
Opportunity to offer unsolicited favor or concession.

options.name: Leverage Commitment, Consistency, and Dissonance
options.description: Guide the persuadee to make initial commitments, prompting escalation and, where inconsistencies arise, enable attitude or behavior change to restore consistency.

goal.objective: Secure initial and escalating commitments and motivate attitude/behavior change via consistency and dissonance mechanisms.

success_levels.ideal: Persuadee makes initial and larger commitments, or changes attitude/behavior to restore consistency.
success_levels.acceptable: Some initial commitments or partial discrepancy resolution.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Persuadee refuses to commit or ignores inconsistencies.

goal.reward_hint: Commitments are made and reaffirmed; persuadee demonstrates attitude, intention, or behavior change in line with commitments.

states: Persuadee is undecided, ambivalent, or faces attitude-behavior discrepancy.
Initial commitment can be elicited or history of commitment exists.
Opportunity for escalation or dissonance reduction is present.

options.name: Social Proof and Norm Activation
options.description: Present evidence that others endorse or perform the desired behavior to induce conformity and internalize social norms.

goal.objective: Increase compliance and attitude change via perceived group approval, majority behavior, and salient social norms.

success_levels.ideal: Persuadee recognizes and internalizes group endorsement, conforming in action or attitude.
success_levels.acceptable: Persuadee is influenced by, but not fully convinced due to, group cues.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Persuadee rejects social proof or norm cues as irrelevant or manipulative.

goal.reward_hint: Persuadee references group behaviors, testimonials, or norms as influential.

states: Norms are salient, ambiguous, or misperceived.
Persuadee requests, references, or is open to group evidence.
Persuader seeks to leverage conformity or internalization.

options.name: Invoking Authority and Building Credibility
options.description: Influence by leveraging expertise, authority, likability, similarity, and trust to enhance message acceptance.

goal.objective: Prompt compliance and increase persuasion through displayed credibility, trustworthiness, and relatability.

success_levels.ideal: Persuadee trusts and complies due to persuader’s credibility and affinity.
success_levels.acceptable: Persuadee questions but is influenced by authority or likability cues.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Persuadee rejects authority, expertise, or dislikes persuader.

goal.reward_hint: Persuadee cites authority, expertise, or affinity as justification for compliance or agreement.

states: Persuader's expertise, credentials, or identity are relevant.
Persuadee expresses skepticism, low trust, or group identity matters.
Need for enhanced credibility, likability, or attractiveness.

options.name: Scarcity and Urgency Framing
options.description: Increase perceived value and urgency by presenting opportunities, resources, or information as rare or limited.

goal.objective: Drive compliance and quick decision-making by leveraging psychological reactance and urgency.

success_levels.ideal: Persuadee acts quickly and decisively to secure scarce opportunity.
success_levels.acceptable: Heightened interest is observed but action is delayed.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Scarcity framing is ignored; no added motivation.

goal.reward_hint: Persuadee reacts urgently or expresses fear of missing out.

states: Persuadee perceives abundance or lacks motivation.
Opportunity can be credibly framed as exclusive, time-limited, or competitive.
Susceptibility to urgency or loss aversion is detected.

options.name: Strategic Request Escalation
options.description: Structure persuasion via phased escalation (e.g., foot-in-the-door, door-in-the-face) to maximize compliance over time.

goal.objective: Increase compliance by sequencing requests for optimal psychological impact.

success_levels.ideal: Persuadee complies with both initial and major requests.
success_levels.acceptable: Persuadee agrees to some requests but resists escalation.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Both initial and escalated requests are rejected.

goal.reward_hint: Major compliance following agreement to smaller or previously refused request.

states: Need to move from minor to major compliance.
Resistance to main request; sequential strategy advantageous.
In phased advocacy, negotiation, or fundraising.

options.name: Manage Resistance and Reactance
options.description: Anticipate, recognize, and strategically address resistance, defensive processing, or reactance by adapting strategies and reframing dialogue.

goal.objective: Reduce resistance, maintain dialogue, and restore progress toward persuasion.

success_levels.ideal: Resistance dissipates and compliance or consideration resumes.
success_levels.acceptable: Resistance is contained but dialogue remains open.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Resistance escalates, leading to refusal.

goal.reward_hint: Active opposition lessens or persuadee resumes meaningful consideration.

states: Persuadee displays explicit or implicit resistance.
Signs of psychological reactance or disengagement.
Risk of dialog breakdown.

options.name: Affective and Evaluative Conditioning
options.description: Shift attitudes by associating targets with positive or negative emotional cues, managing mood, or controlling context.

goal.objective: Alter attitudes or change receptivity by pairing targets with affective cues, using mood management or associative mechanisms.

success_levels.ideal: Target attitudes are shifted meaningfully via strong affective associations.
success_levels.acceptable: Moderate attitude change or increased receptivity due to affective cues.
success_levels.unsuccessful: No attitude change or reinforcement of undesired attitudes.

goal.reward_hint: Persuadee’s evaluation or emotions shift toward target direction.

states: Emotional mechanisms (conditioning, mood, fear) are relevant.
Attitude is open to associative or affective change.

options.name: Facilitating Attitude–Behavior Change and Maintenance
options.description: Monitor and guide attitude–behavior links, support intention formation, and reinforce action and maintenance through planning and follow-up.

goal.objective: Foster congruence between attitudes and behavior and reinforce long-term behavior change.

success_levels.ideal: Persuadee’s behavior changes in line with attitudes and is sustained.
success_levels.acceptable: Intention is formed, but action is not yet fully enacted.
success_levels.unsuccessful: No behavioral change despite attitude shift.

goal.reward_hint: Shift in expressed intention or actual behavior; evidence of sustained change.

states: Persuadee indicates openness or has changed attitude; intention or behavior adoption is the goal.
Planning, action, or maintenance phases.

options.name: Stage-Matched Behavioral Change Facilitation
options.description: Guide persuadee through behavioral change stages with stage-appropriate interventions to enable and sustain progress.

goal.objective: Promote progression through precontemplation, contemplation, planning, action, and maintenance stages to achieve sustained behavior change.

success_levels.ideal: Persuadee smoothly advances through stages and sustains behavior change.
success_levels.acceptable: Partial stage progress or initiation of planning/action.
success_levels.unsuccessful: No progress or regression to earlier stages.

goal.reward_hint: Stage advancement or sustained new behavior in line with stage-appropriate support.

states: Persuadee is in a definable behavioral change stage.
Ready for stage-appropriate intervention.

options.name: Post-Persuasion Outcome Assessment
options.description: Evaluate persuadee outcomes—attitude, intention, or behavior change—after intervention and adjust strategies accordingly.

goal.objective: Determine effectiveness of persuasion by measuring shifts in attitudes, intentions, or behaviors.

success_levels.ideal: Sustained, measurable increase in target attitude or behavior.
success_levels.acceptable: Moderate or transient shift observed.
success_levels.unsuccessful: No observable impact or negative shift.

goal.reward_hint: Reported improvement or change in attitudes, intentions, or behaviors following persuasion.

states: Intervention or message delivery is complete.
Persuadee’s change can be observed, measured, or reported.

micro_actions.name: Ask Direct Evaluative Questions or Self-Report
micro_actions.description: Ask persuadee to state opinions, evaluations, or feelings about the target object or behavior (“How do you feel about X?”).
states: Initial attitude assessment phase.

states: Suspect implicit, guarded, or socially sensitive attitudes.

micro_actions.name: Elicit or Clarify Attitude Function or Motive
micro_actions.description: Ask why the attitude is held (“What matters to you about this?” “Whose opinion matters most?”).

micro_actions.name: Prompt Comparative Judgments and Contextual Variation
micro_actions.description: Invite persuadee to compare alternatives or describe attitude across contexts or groups.

micro_actions.name: Observe Behavioral and Nonverbal Cues
micro_actions.description: Monitor reaction time, expressions, and spontaneous reactions to infer implicit or accessible attitudes.

micro_actions.name: Clarify Normative and Control Beliefs
micro_actions.description: Probe for social norm perceptions and perceived behavioral control or barriers.
states: Social influence or logistical factors may play a role.

micro_actions.name: Identify Behavioral Change Stage
micro_actions.description: Ask stage-matching questions to infer readiness for change.
states: Behavioral intervention planned, need for staging.

micro_actions.name: Check Comprehension of Assessment Questions
micro_actions.description: Ensure persuadee understands queries as intended.
states: Uncertainty about persuadee's comprehension.

primitiveGroups.name: Tailoring Message Content and Framing
primitiveGroups.description: Adapt persuasive messaging to match the persuadee’s attitude functions, motives, beliefs, and preferences for optimal impact.

goal.objective: Increase persuasive effectiveness by aligning message content, framing, and style to the persuadee’s dominant motives and attitude structure.

success_levels.ideal: Message is perfectly matched to key functions, values, or determinants, maximizing persuasive impact.
success_levels.acceptable: Message aligns with some relevant characteristics, improving receptivity.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Message is mismatched, ignored, or rejected; triggers resistance.

goal.reward_hint: Persuadee’s engagement, involvement, and positive processing are increased; message is viewed as relevant.

states: Attitude functions, beliefs, or motivational basis have been identified.
Time to construct the intervention or select content and framing.
Generic strategies are not sufficient.

micro_actions.name: Diagnose and Match Attitude Function
micro_actions.description: Ask targeted questions to clarify dominant attitude function and select arguments that fit (e.g., utilitarian, value-expressive, social).
states: Identifying attitude function to align message.

micro_actions.name: Frame Information or Arguments for Personal Relevance
micro_actions.description: Connect message elements to persuadee’s goals, values, or context.
states: Heightening motivation or demonstrating practical relevance.

micro_actions.name: Adjust Message Complexity and Style
micro_actions.description: Tailor detail and tone (simple/complex, formal/informal, narrative/statistical) to audience expectations or elaboration likelihood.
states: Persuadee’s engagement level or preferences are known.

micro_actions.name: Visual, Verbal, or Symbolic Cues
micro_actions.description: Use artifacts, graphics, or language to reinforce match to function, norm, or value.
states: Seeking to reinforce attitude function and salience.

primitiveGroups.name: Engagement and Persuasive Message Delivery
primitiveGroups.description: Present the main persuasive content using tactical structures, narratives, rationales, sequential requests, and strategic framing.

goal.objective: Deliver persuasive content that achieves attitudinal or behavioral shift toward the intended goal.

success_levels.ideal: Persuadee is engaged and favorably evaluates the message, leading to desired change.
success_levels.acceptable: Persuadee attends to the message and considers the proposal.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Persuadee disregards, resists, or reacts negatively to the message.

goal.reward_hint: Evidence of persuadee engagement, elaboration, or positive attitudinal movement.

states: Persuadee is primed or ready for new information.
Message is tailored and ready for delivery.
Initial assessment and tailoring phases have passed.

micro_actions.name: Explicitly State or Clarify the Advocated Position
micro_actions.description: Present the main recommendation, attitude, or action unambiguously.
states: Need to ensure clarity on position.

micro_actions.name: Deliver Strong Central Arguments or Peripheral Cues
micro_actions.description: Match message strength and features to engage elaboration or cue-based processing as suitable.
states: Route of processing has been determined.
Matching message elements to engagement level.

micro_actions.name: Present Narrative, Example, or Testimonial
micro_actions.description: Use stories, cases, or testimonies for identification or deeper engagement.
states: Narrative likely improves message impact.
Factual arguments insufficient for engagement.

micro_actions.name: Frame Consequences as Gain/Loss Aligned to Values
micro_actions.description: Describe anticipated outcomes using gain/loss framing, aligned with most salient values.
states: Outcome framing impacts persuasion.
Values or risk salience is high.

micro_actions.name: Solicit Self-Generated Advocacy or Commitment
micro_actions.description: Encourage persuadee to articulate reasons or advocate for the position, increasing internalization.
states: Persuadee is receptive; further commitment is sought.

micro_actions.name: Deliver Concrete Behavioral Recommendations
micro_actions.description: Specify actionable, clear steps for persuadee to follow.
states: Persuadee readiness for action is high.

primitiveGroups.name: Reciprocity Initiation
primitiveGroups.description: Initiate dialogue by creating a sense of indebtedness in the persuadee through unsolicited favors or concessions.

goal.objective: Trigger the persuadee's desire to reciprocate and increase compliance by establishing obligation.

success_levels.ideal: Persuadee feels indebted and predisposed to comply with subsequent requests.
success_levels.acceptable: Persuadee acknowledges the favor and exhibits moderate inclination to reciprocate.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Persuadee does not value or recognize the favor.

goal.reward_hint: Signs of gratitude, indebtedness, or willingness to reciprocate.

states: Beginning of interaction.
Persuadee has not yet received a request.
Opportunity to offer unsolicited favor or concession.

micro_actions.name: Offer Unsolicited Gift or Favor
micro_actions.description: Provide something valuable to persuadee without prior request.
states: Initial contact before making requests.

micro_actions.name: Explicitly Label the Favor
micro_actions.description: Emphasize the personal nature of the gift or act.
states: After providing unsolicited favor.

micro_actions.name: Persist Gently if Refused
micro_actions.description: Politely insist on acceptance if initially refused.
states: Gift or favor is declined at first.

micro_actions.name: Reference the Favor When Making Request
micro_actions.description: Mention or imply previous gift or kindness when transitioning to a request.
states: Moving from favor-giving to explicit request.
Persuadee has acknowledged favor.

primitiveGroups.name: Leverage Commitment, Consistency, and Dissonance
primitiveGroups.description: Guide the persuadee to make initial commitments, prompting escalation and, where inconsistencies arise, enable attitude or behavior change to restore consistency.

goal.objective: Secure initial and escalating commitments and motivate attitude/behavior change via consistency and dissonance mechanisms.

success_levels.ideal: Persuadee makes initial and larger commitments, or changes attitude/behavior to restore consistency.
success_levels.acceptable: Some initial commitments or partial discrepancy resolution.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Persuadee refuses to commit or ignores inconsistencies.

goal.reward_hint: Commitments are made and reaffirmed; persuadee demonstrates attitude, intention, or behavior change in line with commitments.

states: Persuadee is undecided, ambivalent, or faces attitude-behavior discrepancy.
Initial commitment can be elicited or history of commitment exists.
Opportunity for escalation or dissonance reduction is present.

micro_actions.name: Prompt for Small Commitment
micro_actions.description: Request minor verbal, written, or behavioral agreement (e.g., answering a question, signing, or stating a goal).
states: Initial conversation, persuadee is hesitant.

micro_actions.name: Elicit Public or Written Statements
micro_actions.description: Encourage commitments to be stated clearly, publicly, or in writing.
states: Verbal or private agreement has been secured.

micro_actions.name: Tie Current Request to Previous Commitments
micro_actions.description: Reference past agreements to justify escalation to a larger request.
states: Escalation from minor to more substantial requests.

micro_actions.name: Highlight Discrepancy and Prompt Consistency
micro_actions.description: Point out inconsistencies between attitudes and actions or between old and new commitments, guiding resolution.
states: Evidence of inconsistency or commitment violation.

micro_actions.name: Offer Resolution Pathways (Attitude or Behavior Change)
micro_actions.description: Suggest concrete steps, self-affirmation, or acknowledgment to restore consistency.
states: Persuadee seeks to resolve dissonance.

primitiveGroups.name: Social Proof and Norm Activation
primitiveGroups.description: Present evidence that others endorse or perform the desired behavior to induce conformity and internalize social norms.

goal.objective: Increase compliance and attitude change via perceived group approval, majority behavior, and salient social norms.

success_levels.ideal: Persuadee recognizes and internalizes group endorsement, conforming in action or attitude.
success_levels.acceptable: Persuadee is influenced by, but not fully convinced due to, group cues.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Persuadee rejects social proof or norm cues as irrelevant or manipulative.

goal.reward_hint: Persuadee references group behaviors, testimonials, or norms as influential.

states: Norms are salient, ambiguous, or misperceived.
Persuadee requests, references, or is open to group evidence.
Persuader seeks to leverage conformity or internalization.

micro_actions.name: Cite Majority, Peer, or Group Behavior
micro_actions.description: State that most or similar people engage in target behavior.
states: Persuadee is unsure, seeks social guidance.

micro_actions.name: Present Testimonials or Public Endorsements
micro_actions.description: Share stories of approval, customer stories, or visible examples.
states: Persuadee wants evidence or is skeptical.

micro_actions.name: Highlight Immediate Group or In-group Behavior
micro_actions.description: Point out ongoing, observable actions, or reference in-group members modeling target behavior.
states: Group context present or can be staged.

micro_actions.name: Clarify and Personalize Normative Feedback
micro_actions.description: Compare persuadee's reported attitudes or behaviors to group data; clarify normative distinctions (descriptive vs. injunctive).
states: Correcting misperceptions or increasing norm salience.

micro_actions.name: Reference Similar Others or Subgroups
micro_actions.description: Call out individuals or subgroups with whom persuadee identifies that have adopted the behavior.
states: Social identity, subgroup relevance, or similarity detection.

primitiveGroups.name: Invoking Authority and Building Credibility
primitiveGroups.description: Influence by leveraging expertise, authority, likability, similarity, and trust to enhance message acceptance.

goal.objective: Prompt compliance and increase persuasion through displayed credibility, trustworthiness, and relatability.

success_levels.ideal: Persuadee trusts and complies due to persuader’s credibility and affinity.
success_levels.acceptable: Persuadee questions but is influenced by authority or likability cues.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Persuadee rejects authority, expertise, or dislikes persuader.

goal.reward_hint: Persuadee cites authority, expertise, or affinity as justification for compliance or agreement.

states: Persuader's expertise, credentials, or identity are relevant.
Persuadee expresses skepticism, low trust, or group identity matters.
Need for enhanced credibility, likability, or attractiveness.

micro_actions.name: Display or Mention Credentials and Relevant Experience
micro_actions.description: Make authority or expertise explicit at initial interaction or when legitimacy is in doubt.
states: Skepticism or need for expertise assurance.

micro_actions.name: Reference High-Credibility Sources or Endorsements
micro_actions.description: Cite reputable evidence, studies, or authoritative endorsements.
states: Message needs credibility reinforcement.
Persuadee values trusted information.

micro_actions.name: Mirror Attitudes or Reference Shared Identity
micro_actions.description: Highlight similarities or shared group membership for increased rapport.
states: Rapport or similarity is beneficial.
Group identity is salient.

micro_actions.name: Express Personalized Compliments or Appreciation
micro_actions.description: Offer sincere compliments or acknowledge persuadee’s qualities.
states: Rapport-building phases or when liking needed.

micro_actions.name: Highlight or Feign Similarities
micro_actions.description: Point out shared interests or background; subtly mirror behavior.
states: Persuadee is distant or guarded.

micro_actions.name: Adopt Likable, Warm, and Polite Presentation
micro_actions.description: Use friendly, polite tone and positive affect to lower social distance.
states: Likability will facilitate compliance.

micro_actions.name: Reference Mutual Connections
micro_actions.description: Mention shared acquaintances or affiliations.
states: Opportunity to build warmth and credibility.

micro_actions.name: Acknowledge Message Weaknesses Transparently
micro_actions.description: Admit known drawbacks or limitations to increase trust.
states: Building trust or reduce reactance.

primitiveGroups.name: Scarcity and Urgency Framing
primitiveGroups.description: Increase perceived value and urgency by presenting opportunities, resources, or information as rare or limited.

goal.objective: Drive compliance and quick decision-making by leveraging psychological reactance and urgency.

success_levels.ideal: Persuadee acts quickly and decisively to secure scarce opportunity.
success_levels.acceptable: Heightened interest is observed but action is delayed.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Scarcity framing is ignored; no added motivation.

goal.reward_hint: Persuadee reacts urgently or expresses fear of missing out.

states: Persuadee perceives abundance or lacks motivation.
Opportunity can be credibly framed as exclusive, time-limited, or competitive.
Susceptibility to urgency or loss aversion is detected.

micro_actions.name: Explicitly State Limited Supply or Opportunity
micro_actions.description: Announce restricted availability or last-chance offers.
states: Credible scarcity; persuadee hesitates.

micro_actions.name: Emphasize Imminent Deadlines
micro_actions.description: Reference time-bound offers or expiring opportunities.
states: Inciting urgency needed.

micro_actions.name: Frame as Loss
micro_actions.description: Describe negative consequence if action not taken quickly.
states: Persuadee is undecided or procrastinating.

micro_actions.name: Withhold, Then Reveal Access
micro_actions.description: Temporarily deny, then selectively offer opportunity to prompt immediate commitment.
states: Negotiation nearing close; persuadee wavering.

primitiveGroups.name: Strategic Request Escalation
primitiveGroups.description: Structure persuasion via phased escalation (e.g., foot-in-the-door, door-in-the-face) to maximize compliance over time.

goal.objective: Increase compliance by sequencing requests for optimal psychological impact.

success_levels.ideal: Persuadee complies with both initial and major requests.
success_levels.acceptable: Persuadee agrees to some requests but resists escalation.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Both initial and escalated requests are rejected.

goal.reward_hint: Major compliance following agreement to smaller or previously refused request.

states: Need to move from minor to major compliance.
Resistance to main request; sequential strategy advantageous.
In phased advocacy, negotiation, or fundraising.

micro_actions.name: Make Large Initial Request (Door-in-the-Face)
micro_actions.description: Ask for something substantial first to setup a more reasonable request after refusal.
states: Persuadee is resistant or context allows concession.

micro_actions.name: Follow with Smaller Compromise Request
micro_actions.description: Quickly propose more moderate request after initial refusal.
states: Initial large request declined.

micro_actions.name: Present Sequential Requests (Foot-in-the-Door)
micro_actions.description: Begin with easy/low-threshold request, then gradually escalate.
states: Opportunity for gradual acceptance.

micro_actions.name: Emphasize Concession or Generosity
micro_actions.description: Frame reduction as a concession to obligate reciprocation.
states: After shifting from larger to smaller request.

primitiveGroups.name: Manage Resistance and Reactance
primitiveGroups.description: Anticipate, recognize, and strategically address resistance, defensive processing, or reactance by adapting strategies and reframing dialogue.

goal.objective: Reduce resistance, maintain dialogue, and restore progress toward persuasion.

success_levels.ideal: Resistance dissipates and compliance or consideration resumes.
success_levels.acceptable: Resistance is contained but dialogue remains open.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Resistance escalates, leading to refusal.

goal.reward_hint: Active opposition lessens or persuadee resumes meaningful consideration.

states: Persuadee displays explicit or implicit resistance.
Signs of psychological reactance or disengagement.
Risk of dialog breakdown.

micro_actions.name: Acknowledge and Validate Resistance
micro_actions.description: Recognize objections and show empathy for persuadee's position.
states: Objections or disengagement observed.

micro_actions.name: Reframe or Restate Request
micro_actions.description: Restate request less threateningly or offer alternatives.
states: Persistence of resistance after initial request.

micro_actions.name: Highlight Autonomy and Choice
micro_actions.description: Reassure persuadee that choice is theirs to reduce manipulation perceptions.
states: Reactance or defensiveness detected.

micro_actions.name: Use Polite Insistence or Positivity
micro_actions.description: Maintain friendly tone while gently reiterating request.
states: Tension rising; discussion still open.

micro_actions.name: Prompt Self-Affirmation or Value Reflection

micro_actions.name: Forewarn About Persuasion

states: Risk of perceived manipulation or reactance.

primitiveGroups.name: Affective and Evaluative Conditioning
primitiveGroups.description: Shift attitudes by associating targets with positive or negative emotional cues, managing mood, or controlling context.

goal.objective: Alter attitudes or change receptivity by pairing targets with affective cues, using mood management or associative mechanisms.

success_levels.ideal: Target attitudes are shifted meaningfully via strong affective associations.
success_levels.acceptable: Moderate attitude change or increased receptivity due to affective cues.
success_levels.unsuccessful: No attitude change or reinforcement of undesired attitudes.

goal.reward_hint: Persuadee’s evaluation or emotions shift toward target direction.

states: Emotional mechanisms (conditioning, mood, fear) are relevant.
Attitude is open to associative or affective change.

micro_actions.name: Pair with Positive or Negative Affective Cues
micro_actions.description: Present attitude object alongside positive (or negative) imagery, music, or statements.
states: Goal is evaluative conditioning.

micro_actions.name: Arrange Proximity of Associations
micro_actions.description: Keep valued people or positive events adjacent to the target.
states: Maximizing evaluative conditioning.

micro_actions.name: Monitor and Adjust for Context or Mood
micro_actions.description: Observe affective state and adapt messages accordingly.
states: Mood or context influences message processing.

micro_actions.name: Distract from Overt Persuasion

micro_actions.name: Detect and Manage Negative Associations
micro_actions.description: Watch for negative associations and avoid reinforcing them.
states: Risk of counter-conditioning present.

primitiveGroups.name: Facilitating Attitude–Behavior Change and Maintenance
primitiveGroups.description: Monitor and guide attitude–behavior links, support intention formation, and reinforce action and maintenance through planning and follow-up.

goal.objective: Foster congruence between attitudes and behavior and reinforce long-term behavior change.

success_levels.ideal: Persuadee’s behavior changes in line with attitudes and is sustained.
success_levels.acceptable: Intention is formed, but action is not yet fully enacted.
success_levels.unsuccessful: No behavioral change despite attitude shift.

goal.reward_hint: Shift in expressed intention or actual behavior; evidence of sustained change.

states: Persuadee indicates openness or has changed attitude; intention or behavior adoption is the goal.
Planning, action, or maintenance phases.

micro_actions.name: Elicit Behavioral Intentions
micro_actions.description: Ask persuadee about intention or willingness to act.
states: Tracking link between attitude and behavior.

micro_actions.name: Probe for Control and Barriers
micro_actions.description: Ask about obstacles or support for the behavior.
states: Translating intention to action may pose challenges.

micro_actions.name: Strengthen Intention–Action Consistency
micro_actions.description: Prompt persuadee to specify when, where, and how they will act.
states: Planning or enhancing implementation likelihood.

micro_actions.name: Provide Feedback and Follow-Up
micro_actions.description: Check in on actual behavior after intervention; reinforce or adjust.
states: Post-intervention tracking.

micro_actions.name: Modify Cues and Environment for Support
micro_actions.description: Suggest adjustments in environment or reminders to facilitate change or maintenance.

primitiveGroups.name: Stage-Matched Behavioral Change Facilitation
primitiveGroups.description: Guide persuadee through behavioral change stages with stage-appropriate interventions to enable and sustain progress.

goal.objective: Promote progression through precontemplation, contemplation, planning, action, and maintenance stages to achieve sustained behavior change.

success_levels.ideal: Persuadee smoothly advances through stages and sustains behavior change.
success_levels.acceptable: Partial stage progress or initiation of planning/action.
success_levels.unsuccessful: No progress or regression to earlier stages.

goal.reward_hint: Stage advancement or sustained new behavior in line with stage-appropriate support.

states: Persuadee is in a definable behavioral change stage.
Ready for stage-appropriate intervention.

micro_actions.name: Offer Planning Assistance

states: Contemplation or planning phases.

micro_actions.name: Provide Self-Efficacy and Emotional Support
micro_actions.description: Reinforce confidence and provide encouragement for change and maintenance.

primitiveGroups.name: Post-Persuasion Outcome Assessment
primitiveGroups.description: Evaluate persuadee outcomes—attitude, intention, or behavior change—after intervention and adjust strategies accordingly.

goal.objective: Determine effectiveness of persuasion by measuring shifts in attitudes, intentions, or behaviors.

success_levels.acceptable: Moderate or transient shift observed.
success_levels.unsuccessful: No observable impact or negative shift.

goal.reward_hint: Reported improvement or change in attitudes, intentions, or behaviors following persuasion.

states: After message delivery.

micro_actions.description: Employ pre-vs.-post metrics to quantify change.

micro_actions.description: Ask about actual new actions taken post-conversation.

micro_actions.description: Prompt reflectiveness on what influenced or hindered change.
states: Evaluating effective and ineffective elements.

static_dimensions.dimension_name: Background, Life Context, and Group Identity
static_dimensions.description: Captures the person's history, upbringing, cultural and social influences, long-term group memberships, and formative experiences. Includes how these elements shape worldview, baseline openness or defensiveness, interpretation of persuasive messages, and expectations in persuasion.

static_dimensions.dimension_name: Core Goals, Values, and Motivational Orientations
static_dimensions.description: Summarizes what the person habitually values, wants, or prioritizes, and which dominant needs, motives, or goal orientations typically guide their attitudes, decisions, and reactions to persuasive attempts.

static_dimensions.dimension_name: Attitude Structure, Functions, and Underlying Beliefs
static_dimensions.description: Captures typical organization of attitudes (cognitive, affective, behavioral blend), psychological functions attitudes serve (e.g., utilitarian, value-expressive), influential beliefs that underlie responses, attitude strength, and habitual openness or resistance to attitude change.

Represents stable aspects of self-image (public vs. private identity, self-esteem, identity-based vulnerability), sense of belonging, and desire for consistency or coherence in beliefs and behavior. Informs susceptibility to identity-based influence and dissonance.

Describes the person's preferred style of processing persuasive information (heuristic vs. systematic, analytic vs. intuitive), habitual resistance strategies, and typical emotional or behavioral responses such as skepticism, routine openness, or use of cognitive shortcuts.

Describes baseline habits in willingness to share attitudes, beliefs, motives, or emotions in persuasive settings, including general expressiveness, guardedness, and contextual modifiers (e.g., trust, social safety).
Captures the extent to which behaviors, attitudes, or responses relevant to the persuasion target are habitual, automatic, or consciously intended, influencing openness to change.

Describes baseline situational or enduring constraints (e.g., time pressure, environmental barriers, competing obligations, resource availability), as well as strengths or supports (e.g., resilience, knowledge, social networks) that affect engagement and decision-making.

Captures the person's baseline ability and tendency to recognize, reflect on, and articulate their own motivations, biases, and habitual responses. Shapes openness to self-disclosure or resistance to introspection.

Summarizes stable psychological traits (e.g., need for cognition, sensation-seeking, reactance proneness, self-esteem) that systematically affect engagement, openness, and resistance to persuasive attempts.

dynamic_dimensions.description: Captures the persuadee’s present mental energy, focus, and motivation regarding persuasion (e.g., alert, tired, engaged, ambivalent, resistant, receptive). Indicates current willingness, readiness, or ability to process and respond to persuasive messages.

Represents the person’s dominant and evolving emotional tone or mood during the session (e.g., anxious, enthusiastic, defensive, positive, negative, neutral), which influences receptivity, openness, and defensive responses. Multiple states can co-exist.
Describes moment-to-moment readiness to share thoughts, feelings, attitudes, discomfort, or motives in the session; options include open, guarded, selective, or reluctant states.
Indicates how actively the person is mentally and emotionally involved in the session: attentive, distracted, withdrawn, or unknown.

Captures salient, evolving properties of attitudes toward persuasion targets, such as strength, certainty, extremity, accessibility, ambivalence, attitude function, belief endorsement/rejection, and direction of any attitude change.

Represents the person’s current approach to processing persuasive input—systematic, heuristic, mixed, or level of cognitive elaboration (central vs. peripheral). Determines susceptibility to detailed arguments or cues.

Represents what is presently motivating responses: desire for gain, avoidance of loss, social approval, autonomy, moral action, or topic-specific salience of personal values (e.g., achievement, security, belonging).

dynamic_dimensions.dimension_name: Stage in Change and Intention Formation
dynamic_dimensions.description: Tracks readiness to change and current intention to act, including contemplation, preparation, action, maintenance, or no intention/relapse. Predicts openness to persuasion and likelihood of follow-through.
Represents the person’s present attribution of sincerity, competence, trust, or rapport with the persuader/authority figure, ranging from high trust and collaboration to distrust or suspicion.
Captures current psychological reactance and resistance to influence—ranging from engagement or compliance, through moderate resistance, to oppositional behavior or avoidance.
In group or social contexts, tracks whether the persuadee feels personally accountable (focused) or distributes responsibility to others (diffuse), affecting willingness to act and social influence.
Describes how clearly the persuadee can recognize and articulate their own motivations, attitudes, or biases at this moment, ranging from high reflection to unawareness.
Tracks which group memberships or social identities are currently salient, and how group norms or status affect the individual's thinking and responsiveness.

Applies additional, session-specific factors such as perceived threat and efficacy (for threat/fear appeals), narrative involvement, or motivation to comply with social referents. Only relevant when applicable.

turns.text: Session One on Tuesday evening, the 8th of October, with J.M. So Welcome, Jessa.
Thank you. (laughs)

It is good to have this time with you and I'd like to start off this first session that we're doing by asking you to just say a little more, if you would, about what you had expressed to me a little bit earlier about having some trepidation about the sessions you and I are going to do, given that up until now your therapy has been of a different approach. So please would you say more about what your concern has been, and more importantly, what it is right now.

Sure. Absolutely. The trepidation is that the therapy I've had in the past has been psycho-analytic based and so my trepidation now is that my impression of cognitive behavioral therapy, and the REBT you do, is that you don't really this is just my impression and I could be wrong but that you don't really look into the childhood, so to speak, as much and it's a little bit more just modifying behaviors which, to me, seems wonderful and great. But my trepidation is that that kind of stuff might not be what I'm used to or what may or may not work for me.

Aah. So that's the concern. I think you're quite right when you say that it may not be what you're used to, because it probably isn't what you're used to. Also, the few words you've just expressed now about your impression of what you call CBT, and what we're doing here being rational emotive behavior therapy... which is the pioneering CBT, but it has some very distinct qualities and different emphases. Your words just a few moments ago indicate that you have the impression that there's a large focus on changing behaviors, but really changing behaviors is only one possible aspect of it. The goal, after we clarify your specific goal or goals of what you think you'd like to work on and change for the better, if anything, is to do what works best for you and usually in REBT that includes changing harmful thinking patterns. Now, if you don't have any harmful thinking patterns, we won't work on changing them!
turns.primitiveAction: Explain CBT Model and Treatment Structure

turns.text: No, I do. (laughs)

That's something to explore, and also one of the premises of REBT speaks of the inter-connectedness of behavior and emotions and thinking, so it's really not only about changing behaviors. Yes, it can include changing behaviors if that's going to be to your benefit. However truly speaking, behaviors are influenced by the thoughts and emotions we have, and often a greater focus, especially an initial focus when we do REBT, can be on exploring your thinking and seeing whether it's helping you or hurting you, also teaching you the healthy ways of thinking, which create healthy behaviors in most cases and healthy emotions. I just wanted to clarify what sounded like a misconception about the REBT approach that we will do.
Yes. Got you.

You also mentioned that you don't know if it's for you or not, or if it will help you or not. As you notice, I'm not tying you down with chains (both laugh). If you find that it's not helpful, we can stop.
Okay.

Now in your interest, it will be good for us to explore why you think it's not helpful if, as sessions progress, you ever think that our work is not helpful to you, but of course you're not bound to keep doing this work. You're a free woman and the only reason that I do what I do is to help you and, more importantly, to help you learn how to help yourself feel healthier emotions, think in healthier ways and, as appropriate, behave in healthier ways if you're not behaving in the ways that serve you the best. Does that make sense?
Yes, that makes perfect sense.
Does that alleviate any of your concerns?

Yes, it does. It does. Definitely. I think I have to see it; that's how I think. I'm more of an applying and seeing exactly what it is person, but everything you just said yes, that's very helpful moving forward.
Do you have any other questions about what I do and the approach before we begin?
No. I'm very familiar with therapy in general.
You mean you're familiar with the therapy you've had so far, in general?
Yeah, that so far. I'm pretty familiar with just how therapy, in general, works. Like I said, it was just more about the specific type and I think you answered a lot of that.

Okay. Away we go then! (Both laugh) Now my next question to you, Jessa, is what issues or areas do you want us to look at? What emotions? You already mentioned anxiety, so tell me anything additional about that, and more. What are your goals for our time together?

turns.text: I think probably for me the main thing would be just anxiety, but anxiety specific to having to make life decisions and having anxiety over trust and faith in myself that I'm making the right choices, whatever those choices may be. The reason I'm saying that is because I feel anxiety just in daily life that comes up minute to minute to minute, so I don't really feel like I have specific anxieties like phobias or anything like that. I'm not one of those people that say, "Oh, I'm afraid to go into an elevator. I'm afraid to do this." It's not like that type of thing. It's more of this anxiety of whether I said the right thing or did the right thing or made the right decision and having anxiety over not having the faith in myself to know that I made the right decision. That's basically what I would love to get out of it, to be able to wake up every morning and be like, "I made the right decision." (Laughs) And I'm not always going to feel that way, but if I don't feel that I made the right decision about something, then I'd like not having so much anxiety around it, if that makes sense.
Yes, it makes sense. It appears that you're a very experienced self-torturer.

turns.text: Yes. I am. I love to punish myself. No, I'm joking. I don't, but that's what I do. (chuckles)
Well it sounds like we're semi-joking, but in all seriousness . . .
